title: Matcha shortbread
subtitle: buttery shortbread with matcha stirred through for a green tint and a faintly bitter edge
excerpt: Matcha shortbread is classic butter shortbread with matcha powder worked through the dough, giving a vivid green colour and a clean, slightly bitter note against the sweet butter base. The method is the same as plain shortbread. The matcha flavour is mild in the baked biscuit and works best with a light dusting of icing sugar over the top.
sourceNotes: Matcha shortbread is a British-Japanese hybrid that became popular in British home baking from the 2010s onward as matcha spread from Japanese tea culture into the broader food scene. The shortbread method itself is standard Scottish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked and cooled biscuits in an airtight container for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.

content.text: Matcha shortbread uses the same method as plain butter shortbread, with matcha powder sifted into the flour before rubbing in the butter. The biscuits come out vivid green and have a delicate, slightly bitter edge that offsets the richness of the butter. Sift the matcha carefully to avoid lumps; it disperses better in the dry flour than when added to the butter.
Sift together the flour, matcha powder, and icing sugar into a bowl. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs and is beginning to hold together.

Bring the dough together by pressing it with your hands. It will be crumbly at first but should hold a shape when squeezed. Turn onto a lightly floured surface and press into a flat disc. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 160 degrees C (fan 140 degrees C / gas 3). Line two baking trays with baking paper.
Roll the chilled dough to about 5 mm thick and cut into rounds or rectangles with a biscuit cutter. Place on the prepared trays with a little space between each. Re-roll the trimmings once.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes until the biscuits are set and just beginning to colour very slightly at the edges. They will still feel soft but will firm up on cooling.
Leave on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack. Dust with icing sugar once cooled.

attrs.problem: Biscuits turning brown rather than staying green
attrs.avoid: Avoid baking at too high a temperature or for too long; browning destroys the green colour of the matcha.
attrs.fix: Keep the oven low (160 degrees C maximum) and remove the biscuits as soon as the edges just begin to lose their raw look. The green colour fades further as the biscuits age.

attrs.problem: Dough too crumbly to roll out
attrs.avoid: Avoid working the dough too little; under-worked shortbread does not hold together well enough to roll.
attrs.fix: Press the dough together firmly with your hands for a minute longer, working it gently until it just coheres. If still crumbly, add half a teaspoon of cold water and press again.
